summary: Assess WBGT exposure, plan worker controls, and investigate heat illness. Explore the five-day course and practical curriculum.
lede: Workplace heat stress training helps OHS teams, site supervisors, and occupational-health practitioners assess hot-work exposure and plan controls that protect workers. Learners practise recording WBGT readings, building heat-risk registers, setting acclimatisation and work-rest schedules, checking hydration and vulnerable-worker safeguards, and documenting heat-illness investigations with field scenarios and Excel templates for site planning and review.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess hot-work exposure, supervise field controls, support worker health, or inspect workplace heat protections across outdoor and industrial operations.
prerequisites: Basic OHS or site-safety experience is recommended. No coding is required; bring a laptop with Excel access for template-based exercises. Specialist physiological monitoring and ISO 7933 calculations are covered at an introductory interpretation level.
